title: Thank God Camels Can't Fly
source: The Turkish Jester, tr. George Borrow (1884)
lesson: Be grateful for the problems you don't have.
lines: One day, Nasreddin stood up in the town square with a very serious face. Everyone leaned in, expecting great wisdom.
My friends, today let us give thanks for something truly very important.
Let us give thanks that camels do not have wings! The crowd blinked. Nobody had been thinking about wings.
Imagine if they did. They would perch on your roofs, all day long, burping.
Your chimneys would collapse. Your houses would fall on your heads! Your tea would spill!
The crowd looked up at the sky nervously. Then back at their roofs. Then, very quickly, they gave thanks.
Silly? Yes. But we rarely thank God for the disasters that never happened. Be grateful for the problems you don't have.
Next episode: the stars over Belgrade. Follow so you don't miss it!
